blocks.title:
Three ways we work.
One way we behave.
blocks.sub: Whichever you pick, you get the same people, the same scope-first habit and the same fortnightly review. The detail below is the detail we would put in the SOW.

blocks.title: Engineers inside your team
blocks.sub: Your standups, your board, your repo, your definition of done. We manage the person; you direct the work.
aside: What you get
A named senior engineer, in your standup from day one
Your tooling, your repo, your board — nothing of ours to adopt
We manage performance, holidays and cover; you manage the work
If it is not working, a replacement inside ten working days
Good for
— Scaling a team without a six-month hiring round
— A nine-month push with a hard date
— Covering a leaver while you hire properly
rows: from [YOUR RATE] / day · 3-month minimum · 30 days’ notice

blocks.title: A product, scoped and shipped
blocks.sub: A written scope, a fixed first increment, working software inside six weeks. Then we keep going or we hand it over.
aside: What you get
A two-page SOW three days after the call: in, out, cost
A fixed first increment, six weeks, in your cloud account
A fortnightly review: shipped, slipped, cost against plan
A handover pack: runbook, tests, a recorded walkthrough
Good for
— A new product or module with a deadline
— A rebuild the in-house team cannot fit in
— An MVP that has to survive its first customers
rows: Quoted after the call · NET 14 · IP yours on payment

blocks.title: Systems that stay correct
blocks.sub: Pipelines, warehouses, retrieval and evaluation harnesses. We measure the thing before we claim it improved.
aside: What you get
Ingest and warehouse work that the in-house team can run after
Retrieval and LLM features with an evaluation harness, not a demo
Dashboards people stop arguing with
A before-and-after measurement on every increment
Good for
— Reporting nobody trusts
— A nightly batch that is now a daily problem
— An AI feature that has to be right, not impressive

blocks.title: Eight things we do, in detail.
aside: One page each

blocks.title: Inside every engagement.
aside: Not extras. Not line items.
rows: Every change reviewed by a second senior before it lands.
Tests and a pipeline before the first feature, not after the first incident.
On-call steps and rollback written as we go, in your wiki.
Decisions recorded where your team will find them.
Secrets, access, dependencies: handled, and listed in the handover.
A recorded walkthrough and a week of questions answered, included.

blocks.title: What we work in.
aside: Only what we have shipped to production
rows: Not on the list? We will say so on the call, rather than learn it on your time.

blocks.title: How an engagement runs.
aside: See it play out →
rows: You describe the problem. We say on the call whether we are right for it, and what it would cost.
A two-page SOW: what is in, what is out, what it costs. Before you pay anything.
Access, first commit. You meet the engineers before they start, and they are in your standup from day one.
Working software in your environment, measured before we claim it improved.
Shipped, slipped, cost against plan. Continue, or hand over. Your call, every fortnight.

blocks.title: Tell us the problem. We will tell you which of the three it is.
blocks.sub: Bring the problem, not a brief. If it is outside what we do well, we will say which of our contacts to call instead.
blocks.emailLine: Or email [HELLO@HOPSIG.COM] — reply within one working day.
